recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the approved FHIR-34324 clarification in the active OperationDefinition source and avoids divergent generated/rendered versus conformance guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-34324 asked whether $validate should always return 200 OK when a resource is invalid. The Published/Not Persuasive with Modification resolution clarified that 200 is appropriate when validation could be performed, regardless of validation issues, but content errors such as invalid character sets or broken JSON can make the overall operation fail with a 4xx or 5xx response.
initial_application: Commit 6da05ac1f1fe5ad00535a873c3dfa112ab64e0fd from PR #1804 applied the issue to source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-validate.xml by changing the build footer markdown, but the OperationDefinition comment field still carried the older unconditional 200 OK wording in the current source.
additional_context: Resource is active infrastructure content in source/fhir.ini and source/resource/list-Resource-operations.xml references OperationDefinition/Resource-validate. Later FHIR-37626 work touched the same footer/comment text for endpoint-path clarification and left the old status-code sentence in the comment, while the footer retained the corrected FHIR-34324 sentence. FHIR-I minutes confirm the 2022-03-21 disposition, and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence discussion was found.
reconciliation: Changed source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-validate.xml so the OperationDefinition comment uses the same clarified 200 response guidance already present in the footer. No other policy or endpoint-path text was changed.
source_changes: source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-validate.xml: replaced the old OperationDefinition comment sentence saying $validate returns 200 OK whether or not the resource is valid with the approved clarification that 200 applies when validation can be performed, while certain content errors may fail with 4xx/5xx.
